title: Photography & Videography
tagline: Exposure, light, composition and video, Dubai's rules on filming people and drones, and turning photos into paid work.

superpower.name: Lens Master
superpower.description: Shoots like a pro: better posts and more from photo and video jobs.

syllabus: Week 1: Exposure: aperture, shutter speed and ISO
Week 3: Video: frame rates, motion and sound
Week 4: The law, the business and your portfolio

weeks.title: Exposure
weeks.objective: Control how bright, sharp and blurred your photos are with the exposure triangle.

slides.title: The Exposure Triangle
slides.body: Every exposure is a balance of three settings. Change one and you must adjust another to keep the same brightness.
bullets: Aperture (f-number): how wide the lens opens. f/1.8 is wide (blurry background); f/11 is narrow (everything sharp)
Shutter speed: how long light hits the sensor. 1/1000 s freezes action; 1/30 s blurs motion
ISO: sensor sensitivity. Low ISO (100) is clean; high ISO (3200+) is brighter but grainy
One 'stop' doubles or halves the light
slides.example:
The Sunny 16 rule for bright Dubai sun: at f/16, set the shutter to 1 ÷ ISO.
• ISO 100: f/16 at 1/100 s
• Want a blurry background? Open to f/4 (4 stops more light), so speed up 4 stops: 1/1600 s.
slides.takeaway: Choose the creative setting first (blur or freeze), then balance the others.

slides.title: Focus and Sharpness
slides.body: Sharp photos come from focusing on the right thing and holding the camera steady.
bullets: Focus on the eyes in portraits
Hand-held: keep the shutter at least 1 ÷ focal length (1/50 s for a 50 mm lens)
Tripod for night skylines and long exposures
Phones: tap to focus, and hold to lock exposure
slides.takeaway: If the eyes are sharp, the portrait works.

lab.title: Exposure Lab
lab.brief: Shoot the same scene three ways: frozen action, motion blur and a blurred background, noting the settings.
lab.deliverable: Three photos with aperture, shutter and ISO for each.
lab.proTip: Shoot in aperture priority (A/Av) while learning: you choose the blur, the camera handles the rest.

caseStudy.scenario: You're shooting a fast-moving jet ski at Kite Beach and every photo is blurred. What do you change?

options.text: A faster shutter speed, around 1/1000 s or more.
options.explanation: Fast shutter speeds freeze fast action.
Lower ISO darkens the photo without freezing motion.

quiz.question: Which aperture gives the blurriest background?
quiz.explanation: A wide aperture (small f-number) gives shallow depth of field.

quiz.question: What does high ISO add?
quiz.explanation: High ISO brightens but adds noise.

weeks.title: Light and Composition
weeks.objective: Use natural light and composition rules to make striking images.

slides.title: Working With Light
slides.body: Light makes the photo. Dubai's midday sun is harsh and overhead; the best light is at golden hour, just after sunrise and before sunset, and blue hour after sunset for skylines.
bullets: Golden hour: soft, warm, flattering light
Midday: find open shade or use a reflector
Blue hour: city lights and the sky balance (great for the Burj Khalifa)
Backlight with a reflector for glowing portraits
slides.takeaway: Shoot at the right time and half the work is done.

slides.title: Composition
slides.body: Composition guides the viewer's eye. A few principles make most photos stronger.
bullets: Rule of thirds: put the subject on a third line, not dead centre
Leading lines: roads, railings and the Metro track pull the eye in
Frame within a frame: arches, windows and doorways (great in Al Fahidi)
Simplify: fill the frame and remove clutter
slides.takeaway: Every good photo has one clear subject.

lab.title: Golden Hour Lab
lab.brief: Shoot a portrait and a cityscape at golden hour and at midday, using the rule of thirds and leading lines.
lab.deliverable: Four photos comparing the light, with notes.
lab.proTip: Arrive 30 minutes early: golden hour is short.

caseStudy.scenario: A client wants outdoor portraits in July at 1pm. What do you suggest?

options.explanation: Harsh overhead light and dangerous heat.

options.text: Move to golden hour, or shoot in open shade or indoors with window light.
options.explanation: Better light and safer for everyone.
Direct flash in sun is harsh and unflattering.

quiz.question: When is golden hour?
options: Just after sunrise and before sunset
quiz.explanation: Golden hour is the soft light near sunrise and sunset.

quiz.question: The rule of thirds places the subject:
options: On a third line or intersection
quiz.explanation: Off-centre on thirds is more dynamic.

weeks.title: Video
weeks.objective: Shoot smooth, cinematic video with clean sound.

slides.title: Frame Rates and the 180° Rule
slides.body: Video is many photos a second. Frame rate sets the feel; shutter speed sets the motion blur.
bullets: 24 or 25 fps: the cinematic look
30 fps: social media and TV
60 fps or more: smooth slow motion
180° rule: shutter = 1 ÷ (2 × frame rate)
Use ND filters outdoors to keep the right shutter in bright sun
slides.example:
Filming at 25 fps: shutter = 1 ÷ (2 × 25) = 1/50 s.
In bright sun at 1/50 s the image is too bright, so add an ND filter instead of raising the shutter speed (which makes motion look jittery).
slides.takeaway: Pick the frame rate for the story, then set the shutter to match.

slides.title: Sound and Stability
slides.body: Viewers forgive average video but not bad sound. Use a microphone close to the speaker and keep shots steady.
bullets: A lapel mic for interviews
Record 10 seconds of room tone for editing
Gimbal or tripod for steady shots
Plan shots: wide, medium, close-up
slides.takeaway: Good audio makes average video watchable.

lab.title: Mini Film Lab
lab.brief: Shoot and edit a 60-second story about a place in Dubai, with wide, medium and close-up shots and clean audio.
lab.deliverable: A 60-second edit and a shot list.
lab.proTip: Shoot 3 times more than you need: editing is choosing.

caseStudy.scenario: Your interview footage looks great but the AC noise drowns the voice. What's the fix next time?

options.text: Turn up the volume in editing.
options.explanation: That makes the noise louder too.

options.text: Use a lapel mic close to the speaker and, if allowed, switch off the AC while recording.
options.explanation: Close mics and less background noise mean clean audio.

quiz.question: Which frame rate gives smooth slow motion?
quiz.explanation: Higher frame rates slow down smoothly.

weeks.title: Law, Business and Portfolio
weeks.objective: Shoot within UAE law, price your work and build a portfolio that wins clients.

slides.title: Filming People and Drones in the UAE
slides.body: UAE privacy laws make photographing or filming people without their consent, and sharing it, a serious offence. Drones must be registered and flown only where permitted.
bullets: Get consent before photographing people, and written releases for commercial use
Never share photos of people (especially women and children) without permission
Avoid government buildings, military sites and airports
Drones: register with the aviation authority and fly only in permitted zones
slides.takeaway: In the UAE, consent first is not just polite, it's the law.

slides.title: Pricing and Portfolio
slides.body: Photographers usually charge by the hour, the day or the package, plus editing time and usage rights.
bullets: Day rate: covers shooting, editing, gear and your experience
Usage rights: social media only costs less than a billboard campaign
Portfolio: your 15 best images in one style
Contracts: deliverables, deadline, payment terms
slides.example:
Quoting a café's social media shoot:
• Half-day shoot (4 hours): AED 1,500
• Editing 30 photos: AED 600
• Social media usage for 12 months: included
Total: AED 2,100, 50% deposit to book.
slides.takeaway: Clients buy confidence: a focused portfolio and a clear contract give it.

lab.title: Portfolio Lab
lab.brief: Build a 15-image portfolio in one niche (food, portraits, property or events) and write a one-page price list.
lab.deliverable: A portfolio link and a price list.
lab.proTip: Pick a niche: 'Dubai food photographer' is easier to hire than 'photographer'.

caseStudy.scenario: You took a great street photo of a family at the Dubai Mall fountain. Can you post it on your public Instagram?

options.explanation: UAE law protects people's privacy even in public places.

options.text: Only with their consent; otherwise don't publish it.
options.explanation: Ask permission, or don't post identifiable people.

options.text: Yes, if you add a filter.

quiz.question: Before posting a photo of someone, you need:
quiz.explanation: Consent is required under UAE privacy law.

quiz.question: What raises a photographer's price?
quiz.explanation: Wider usage, like billboards, is worth more.

questions.question: A wide aperture is shown as:
questions.explanation: A small f-number is a wide aperture.

questions.question: Sunny 16 at ISO 200 is f/16 at:
Leading lines:
options: Guide the eye into the photo

questions.question: At 24 fps the 180° shutter is about:
An ND filter:
options: Cuts light so you can keep the right shutter

questions.question: For clean interview audio use:
options: A lapel mic close to the speaker

questions.question: Flying a drone in the UAE requires:
questions.explanation: Drones must be registered and flown legally.

questions.question: A focused portfolio should be:
options: About 15 best images in one niche
questions.explanation: Show your best work in one style.
